p: AirHop sits on the south-western side of Lincoln, which is handy because some cracking green spaces are on the same side of the city. Hartsholme Country Park has a big lake, woodland paths and a play area, and it's a lovely place to unwind after a session. A little further out, Whisby Nature Park is a patchwork of lakes and reedbeds that is brilliant for spotting birds and dragonflies.

Most visitors head uphill for the castle and the cathedral, and rightly so. Inside the castle, you can see one of only four surviving originals of the 1215 Magna Carta, which is a bit of a jaw-dropper when you think about how old it is. Climbing the cobbles of Steep Hill to get there is a challenge in itself, so take it slowly after all that jumping.

On Canwick Hill, the International Bomber Command Centre has a striking memorial spire and exhibitions about the crews of Bomber Command, many of whom flew from airfields in Lincolnshire. It's a moving visit for older children and adults.
The Collection, near the bottom of the hill, mixes archaeology and art, and the Museum of Lincolnshire Life looks at everyday life across the county.
Lincoln's two halves really are uphill and downhill, and parking in the historic quarter can be tight, so many families park lower down and take the walk, or the hop-on bus, up to the top.
Lincoln is also a university city, so term-time weekends can be lively in the centre, and the Brayford area has plenty of family-friendly places to grab a meal.
